A Tale of Two Starts The contest took an unexpected turn in the 33rd minute when a moment of misfortune for Yuto Tsunashima resulted in an own goal , handing Antwerp an early lead. However, any hopes of the hosts cruising were quickly extinguished by a ruthless Standard Liege response. Just five minutes later, Timothe Nkada restored parity, finishing clinically after being set up by Rafiki Said . The visitors' resurgence didn't stop there. In the 42nd minute, David Bates found the back of the net following a precise assist from Casper Nielsen . This quick-fire double completely flipped the script, allowing Standard Liege to head into the halftime interval with a hard-earned lead and the psychological advantage. Rafiki Said Takes Center Stage The second half saw Standard Liege maintain their relentless tempo. Only three minutes after the restart, Rafiki Said turned from provider to scorer, converting a chance created by Adnane Abid . Despite Antwerp attempting to spark a comeback with substitutions—bringing on the likes of Farouck Adekami and Marwan Al-Sahafi —the visitors remained in total control. The decisive blow came in the 62nd minute when Rafiki Said struck again to secure his brace and his team's fourth goal. Late Drama and Red Card As the match entered its final stages, the focus shifted toward tactical management and disciplinary action. Antwerp struggled to find a breakthrough, and frustration began to show, with Zeno Van Den Bosch entering the referee's book. Meanwhile, Standard Liege utilized their bench, introducing Dennis Eckert and Tobias Mohr to see out the result. The drama peaked in the 90th minute when Kiki Kouyate , already on a yellow card from earlier in the half, received his second booking and was subsequently sent off . Despite the late dismissal, the result was never in doubt. The final whistle blew after three minutes of stoppage time, confirming a statement victory for Standard Liege on the road.

Both sides entered the pitch with high ambitions, setting the stage for a tactical battle under the lights. Discipline was tested early, and the referee was forced to reach for his pocket frequently. Thomas Van den Keybus received the first caution just two minutes in, setting a physical tone for the afternoon. He was soon followed into the book by Yuto Tsunashima , Farouck Adekami , and Emin Bayram , as the game became fragmented by tactical fouls. Despite the interruptions, both defenses remained organized, limiting clear-cut chances for much of the first half. Breaking the Deadlock Before the Interval Just as it seemed the teams would head into the break scoreless, a moment of clinical finishing altered the narrative. In the second minute of first-half stoppage time, Rein Van Helden found space in the box to fire KVC Westerlo into the lead. The late goal stunned the home crowd and gave the visitors a crucial psychological advantage heading into the dressing rooms, leaving Antwerp with plenty of work to do in the second period. Fofana Responds for the Hosts The second half saw Antwerp intensify their pressure as they searched for a way back into the game. The turning point arrived in the 64th minute when Modibo Fofana was introduced in place of Gyrano Kerk . The substitution paid dividends almost immediately; in the 69th minute, Fofana latched onto a pass from Daam Foulon to slot home the equalizer. The goal shifted the momentum back to the hosts, who continued to push with fresh legs like Geoffry Hairemans and Gerard Vandeplas . However, despite late tactical changes and four minutes of added time, neither side could find a winner, resulting in a hard-fought draw.
